messages.author: aae8e9f66c6ae74f
messages.subject: spatial model from spBayes
parts:
Hi,

I've been looking at the spBayes package recently, which implements some
nice spatial GLMM methods described here:

Banerjee et al 2008 Gaussian predictive process models for large spatial
data sets J. R. Statist. Soc. B, 70: 825ï¿½848

In this paper they specifically mention the possibility of implementing
their 'predictive process model' using inla (though before the R package
was developed), and I'm wondering if anyone has now done it? It would be
fantastic to fit this sort of model even more efficiently. My guess is
that writing this model for inla is far from trivial (and probably well
beyond my skills!), but if it can be done it would be even more
marvelous to extend it, if possible, to include an observation process
and be able to fit spatially explicit occupancy models.

So, if anyone knows if it's already done, if it's even feasible, and has
an idea of how much programming it woudl take I'd be interested to know.

Thanks!

C

--

messages.author: 715b0b4b1ca68beb
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] spatial model from spBayes
parts:
Not at all! Thanks very much for sending these things, I've been working my way through them all adn think I understand what's going on. In summary for anyone else who reads along later, you've implemented the method (together with the authors) in INLA, but using Matlab code and it's not available in the r-inla package. On the other hand, I've missed the development of the SPDE approach, and as this is already implemented in r-inla I can see why you're not in any hurry to do the other method - from what I can see of the various implementations there are very few problems that Banerjee et al's method can come with that SPDE can't (perhaps slightly more flexible wrt covariance structure, but SPDE has Matern (which covers exponential), so no real shortage of options. It all looks very clever to me. So the final question is how easy would it be to extend the SPDE model to allow for an observation process to fit an occupancy model? In fact, my specific example is simpler than most occupancy models, as the observation process is simply an index of total effort to which I want to fit some decellerating function to estimate probability of detection given presence. (More than!) happy to discuss the more off-line if you're interested...

Thanks very much again - a great help!

Colin

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] spatial model from spBayes

Remember that you need to have the 'testing' version of INLA.
Just do:
inla.upgrade(testing=TRUE)

You should have access to mesh functions after that.

Bests
